questions.q: What is the actual difference between HTTP and HTTPS traffic?
options: HTTP is only for images, HTTPS is only for text
HTTPS uses a completely different request/response model than HTTP
They run over the same port and are indistinguishable
The same request/response exchange, with HTTPS wrapping it in TLS encryption
questions.explain: HTTPS is HTTP's identical request/response conversation, carried inside a TLS-encrypted tunnel so eavesdroppers only see ciphertext.

questions.q: Why does email use SMTP for one direction and POP3 or IMAP for the other?
options: POP3 and IMAP are only used for sending email, never retrieving it
Sending mail (SMTP) and retrieving already-received mail (POP3/IMAP) are different jobs handled by different protocols
Email has always used a single unified protocol for both directions
SMTP and POP3 are two names for the exact same protocol
questions.explain: SMTP sends and relays mail between servers; POP3 and IMAP are separate protocols dedicated to retrieving mail already delivered.

questions.q: What is the key difference between POP3 and IMAP?
options: IMAP can only retrieve one email at a time
POP3 is encrypted by default and IMAP is not
POP3 downloads mail to one device and often deletes it from the server; IMAP keeps the mailbox synced across devices
There is no real difference between them
questions.explain: POP3 is built around a single device pulling mail down; IMAP keeps the mailbox state consistent across every device checking it.

questions.q: Why is SFTP considered the secure replacement for FTP?
options: SFTP and FTP are identical protocols with different names
FTP was never capable of transferring files at all
SFTP tunnels the file transfer through SSH encryption, while plain FTP sends credentials and files unencrypted
SFTP uses a faster but equally insecure transfer method
questions.explain: FTP transmits everything, including login credentials, in plaintext; SFTP protects the same transfer inside SSH's encryption.

questions.q: Why are web, email, and file-transfer services the most commonly attacked protocols on a network?
options: They cannot be monitored or logged by security teams
They're exposed to the widest audience by design, which also makes them the largest attack surface
They are the only protocols that exist on modern networks
Attackers only target protocols running on odd-numbered ports
questions.explain: Because these services are meant to accept input or connections from a broad audience, that same openness is what attackers exploit most.
